usage: Closes a sentence about a noun or a な-adjective in the plain style. Verbs and い-adjectives already end the sentence by themselves.
The polite form is です. The past だった comes from the た-form, not from だ.
Drops before の in noun-modifying: 学生の, not 学生だの.

compare.difference: です is the polite version.
だろう is the guess: "probably is".
